question: Should future `heartbeatTaskState` timestamps be treated as clock-skew/corruption and become due immediately, or should any future timestamp continue to defer the task?
rationale: The code and docs strongly point to `heartbeatTaskState` as last-run state, but merging still changes persisted-state behavior for any existing future timestamp.

options.title: Accept clock-skew guard after proof
options.body: Merge the shared-helper guard after rebase and real proof because documented state is last-run time, not a deferral API.

options.title: Preserve future timestamp deferral
options.body: Ask for a different fix that keeps future timestamps as intentional deferrals, with docs/tests naming that contract.

options.title: Pause until proof/rebase
options.body: Leave the PR open but blocked until the contributor updates against current main and adds real behavior proof.

recommendation.title: Accept clock-skew guard after proof
recommendation.body: Merge the shared-helper guard after rebase and real proof because documented state is last-run time, not a deferral API.
